why: A brief gratitude practice may support well-being for some people. It is optional and is not a treatment for pain.

slides.title: Make Room for Both
slides.content: You can notice something meaningful while also acknowledging pain, frustration, grief, or uncertainty. Gratitude should not erase difficult experiences.

slides.title: Keep It Specific
slides.content: If you want to try it, write one or two specific things you appreciated and why they mattered to you.

slides.title: Results Vary
slides.content: Some people find this useful for attention or well-being; others do not. It is not a test of attitude and you do not need to force positivity.

slides.title: Try It Briefly
slides.content: Write three lines: what happened, why it mattered, and whether you want to repeat or build on it. If you prefer a guided practice, use Kitaro Waga's gratitude meditation section. The full video contains stronger breathwork; practise seated, never while driving or in water, and stop if you feel unwell.

title: Try a brief gratitude practice
